cmi.name: Cummins
cmi.null_note: Cummins discloses no backlog, order-backlog, orders, or book-to-bill metric in its Q2 2026 10-Q (SEC EDGAR, filed 2026-08-04, accession 0000026172-26-000029, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/26172/000002617226000029/cmi-20260630.htm), its matching Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex-99, filed 2026-08-04, accession 0000026172-26-000026, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/26172/000002617226000026/cmi2026q28-kex99.htm), or its Q2 2026 earnings presentation — all checked live 2026-10-04, zero hits for "backlog" or "book-to-bill"; the release speaks of "robust customer orders for standby power for data centers" without a figure. The only comparable aggregate remains the Topic 606 remaining-transaction-price note in the 10-Q ("NOTE 2. REVENUE FROM CONTRACTS WITH CUSTOMERS"), $7.6 billion at June 30, 2026 (up from $6.9 billion at March 31, 2026), for arrangements the note describes as "primarily long-term maintenance agreements, construction contracts, product sales with associated performance obligations extending beyond a year..." — a maintenance-dominated, whole-company aggregate, not an equipment order-backlog metric comparable to peers on this board. Cummins is excluded on this basis.

bloom.disclosure_note: Bloom states a dollar backlog only with its full-year results; its Q1 2026 release (8-K Ex-99.1, filed 2026-04-28) and Q2 2026 release and slides (8-K Ex-99.1/99.2, filed 2026-07-28) give no backlog figure, and on the Q2 2026 call the CEO said only that the backlog is "growing at a faster pace than revenue". The Q2 2026 10-Q's remaining-performance-obligation note ($442.4 million product and installation, $51.7 million service, at June 30, 2026) excludes contracts with an original expected length of one year or less, so it is not comparable with the ~$6 billion product backlog and is not shown.
